html:
Makli is a huge cemetery on a hill near Thatta in southern Sindh, Pakistan, used from about the 14th to the 18th century, when Thatta was the capital of Sindh.

It covers about ten square kilometres and holds hundreds of thousands of graves, among them grand tombs of kings, nobles and saints of the Samma dynasty and the Arghun and Tarkhan rulers who followed, and of Mughal governors. The older stone tombs are carved with dense patterns that blend Hindu, Gujarati and Islamic designs; the later ones are of brick with blue glazed tiles in Persian style.

Thatta declined in the 18th century as the Indus shifted course, and Hyderabad and then Karachi took its place. Makli became a World Heritage Site in 1981. It shows how the Sindh coast lay between the worlds of India, Persia and Central Asia.
sum: Makli is a huge cemetery on a hill near Thatta in southern Sindh, Pakistan, used from about the 14th to the 18th century, when Thatta was the capital of Sindh.
